en.title: Minimum GCD Vulnerability Length After Changing Limited Elements
en.description:
The vulnerability factor is the maximum length of a non-empty contiguous segment whose GCD is greater than 1, or 0 if there is none. You may change at most maxChange elements to any integers; minimize the vulnerability factor. A single element also counts as a contiguous segment.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n maxChange (1≤n≤100000, 0≤maxChange≤n), and the second line contains n integers in 1..10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: change the middle 4 to 1, leaving the longest bad segments 2, 2 and 9, 6 of length 2. Example 2: change the middle to 1, leaving only single-element bad segments on the left and right, so the answer is 1. Example 3: after any two changes there is still an original prime as a single element, so the optimum is 1, not the source's incorrect 0.
hints: Changing an element to 1 is the most useful. Binary search the allowed length L; every window of length L+1 whose original GCD>1 must be hit by a changed position, so greedily, from left to right, change the right end of the first bad window not yet hit. A GCD sparse table answers window queries in O(1).
